data.hypothesis: This remains a one-way 16-byte SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix hybrid, not T1-style whole-buffer validation. The selected parent locates the first high-bit lane in a mixed vector before calling the scalar decoder. Since that vector starts at a known code-point boundary and the scalar decoder already skips ASCII, starting it at the vector boundary may avoid the mask-shifting lane search at the cost of rechecking at most 15 ASCII bytes. The first high-bit byte remains input to strict validation, including when it is a stray continuation. Prior timings motivate the contrast but do not establish its cause; measure on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and official ASCII/malformed boundary checks.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this T2 branch, compare prefix-SIMD/scalar-suffix choices on the official mixed-width input; these measurements do not establish why the variants differed or whether useful ASCII spans are present.
memory_lessons.claim: The 16-byte lane-location parent measured 55.14 µs; a distinct 16-byte prefix/scalar-suffix candidate measured 39.98 µs, a 32-byte variant 47.95 µs, and a 64-byte variant 43.80 µs. All shown outcomes were correct, but the differing sources and three-sample measurements do not isolate a causal effect.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this candidate against the selected parent and baseline using the official n=65536 workload and correctness suite; do not infer benefit from synthetic-only cases.

data.notes: No new measurement or correctness result is claimed; the controller must run the official mixed-width workload and correctness checks. The visible prior candidates were correct, but the measured comparison is limited to the reported runs. Preserve the selected AB-MCTS parent lineage; no integration sources are available.
transformations: Remove the bit-by-bit search for the first high-bit lane; when a complete 16-byte SIMD block contains any high bit, invoke the strict scalar decoder from that block's known code-point boundary.
Skip only complete 16-byte blocks confirmed entirely ASCII; leave tails within n to the scalar decoder and retain exact UTF-8 validity behavior, ABI, output, and thread budget.
